Subject: Renewal kickoff: capacity lanes, uplift asks, and QBR slate

Mark —

Thanks for the time last week. As we discussed, your current commitment window ends in mid-November and we want to kick off the renewal conversation early so there’s no disruption to your production pipelines. High-level items to cover in the kickoff:

- Confirm target term and any headroom (short-term uplift + seasonal lanes)
- Align on QBR agenda and preferred stakeholders
- Document procurement steps (SOW, PO timing, signatures)
- Staffing & runbook for the uplift window

Proposed next steps (quick asks):
1) Can you confirm whether procurement should own the SOW or if we should run a joint draft?
2) Suggested QBR window: week of Oct 18 — two 30–45 minute slots. Do mornings or afternoons work better for your execs?
3) Any hard constraints on start dates for the uplift capacity? We want to avoid overlap with your year-end maintenance window.

I’ve attached a short draft QBR agenda and a mutual action plan csv to help guide the call. Ben will own commercial details and Laura will own the operational/runbook topics.

If you’re open, I’ll propose two calendar slots for the week of Oct 18 and loop in procurement once you confirm the lead.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Grace —

Thanks for the clear note and the docs. Quick answers:

- Procurement should lead the SOW sign-off (they own contract cadence for renewals). I’ve cc’d procurement.
- Week of Oct 18 works; mornings (9:00–11:30 PT) are generally best for our execs.
- We likely need +30% headroom for the first 90 days to support a pilot expansion; exact numbers TBD — our infra team will send an ops snapshot by Friday.

Can you hold two provisional morning slots on Oct 19 and Oct 21? We’ll confirm by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate the proactive coordination.

Best,
